subject.title: fix(approval): distinguish policy vs non-persistable reason when Allow Always unavailable

question: Should maintainers use this PR as the canonical fix for the non-persistable Allow Always wording bug, or choose a different duplicate branch?
rationale: The patch looks correct and proof-backed, but multiple open PRs target the same issue and only a maintainer should choose which branch becomes canonical before closing the rest.

options.title: Use this PR as canonical
options.body: Land this PR after any needed base refresh, then close the duplicate candidate PRs and the linked issue through normal merge/cleanup flow.

options.title: Pick another duplicate branch
options.body: Choose one of the other open candidate PRs only if its larger protocol/API shape is intentionally preferred despite current conflict/proof state.

options.title: Replace with maintainer patch
options.body: Close the contributor candidates and apply a maintainer-owned minimal patch if maintainers want different wording or ownership boundaries.

recommendation.title: Use this PR as canonical
recommendation.body: Land this PR after any needed base refresh, then close the duplicate candidate PRs and the linked issue through normal merge/cleanup flow.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle owns the most recent current-main refactor that controls the exact files this PR now needs to merge through.
